tagline: Two Henrys Fork waterfalls cut through a landscape shaped by volcanoes.
intro: Mesa Falls Scenic Byway follows two-lane paved roads for 28.2 miles between US 20 and Ashton, through the Caribou-Targhee National Forest. Visit Idaho presents the scenic byway through its two waterfalls and volcanic landscape, with viewing platforms and a historic visitor center. Its published driving time is 49 minutes. The upper falls flow over deposits from a volcanic eruption, while the lower falls continue cutting through solidified ash and lava. This is a seasonal drive: in winter, the forest-road section closes to cars and becomes a snowmobile route through the same forest landscape.

The visitor center began with a different purpose. Between 1912 and 1916, the Mesa Power Company built the log-style building that later became the Big Falls Inn and a stage stop. The original inn became an interpretive center. Downstream, the Civilian Conservation Corps built Grandview Overlook in the 1930s, providing a view of Lower Mesa Falls.

Drive south from US 20 on Forest Service Route 294 to Upper and Lower Mesa Falls, then continue toward the old Bear Gulch ski-area site. Idaho 47 leads through Warm River and Marysville into Ashton as Main Street. The forest gives way to the farmland surrounding Ashton at the southern end.

moments.title: Upper Mesa Falls
moments.text: Upper Mesa Falls pours over rock formed from volcanic ash 1.3 million years ago. That compressed, hardened layer is called tuff. Later, the Henrys Fork cut a canyon that lava partly filled; the river then carved its present inner canyon through the basalt. Beside this volcanic landscape, the original Big Falls Inn serves as an interpretive center. The Mesa Power Company built the log-style structure between 1912 and 1916, before it became an inn and stage stop. Paths and viewing areas provide access to views of the upper waterfall.
moments.notice: The falls flow over tuff, rock formed from hardened volcanic deposits.

moments.title: Lower Mesa Falls
moments.text: At Lower Mesa Falls, the Henrys Fork narrows between basalt columns before plunging over the falls. Grandview Overlook provides the view. The Civilian Conservation Corps built it in the 1930s, and the waterfall lies downstream of Upper Mesa Falls in the Caribou-Targhee National Forest. Here, the river continues cutting into solidified ash and lava.
moments.notice: Basalt columns flank the river at the lower falls.

moments.title: Warm River
moments.text: Warm River became an incorporated town in the 1940s for a specific reason: state law restricted liquor licenses to incorporated municipalities, and the small resort community needed to comply. Its population was four in the 2020 census. Idaho 47 passes through town and crosses the river of the same name. Continuing toward Ashton, the highway passes through Marysville before becoming Ashton’s Main Street.
